cells.tense: The shared thing you tend is complete, and your hands are still on it.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: When someone thanks you for keeping a shared thing going, let it land — don't wave it off and don't turn it into the next task.
cells.core:
There's something you keep alive for other people — a practice, a place, a way a group does a thing together — and you can hold it without gripping. You know when a season of work is finished, and you can set the tools down and step back while others take it up. That's not quitting. It's the care completing itself.

After a job like that, what's left is quiet and unused room, and the pull to fill that room with the next project. Let what you did be seen by whoever it was for. Said out loud, it stops needing proof. Stand next to it, take the thanks, and give the work a day off. That's what finishing clean looks like.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish the caring without needing to hold on.
cells.verb: Tending what is growing, by hand, so it holds for whoever comes after
cells.place: Where meaning is passed between people and kept alive by use

cells.tense: You are already at work on something that has not been handed to you yet.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Pick something you keep going that already works, use it as it stands for an evening, and stop improving it.
cells.core:
You tend what's shared, and lately the work runs ahead of what exists. You're maintaining the version after the next repair, the one that will finally be right, while the version here gets no enjoyment at all. It reads as care from inside you. From outside it looks as though nothing may rest, and the shared thing keeps being rebuilt instead of used.

Smaller than it sounds: let a finished piece stay finished. Spend an evening with what you've already kept alive, exactly as it stands, alongside the people it's for. Don't fix it. Don't correct what you notice. Your grip loosens when it can stand without you holding it up. It is already holding. Find that out by standing in it.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a version of it nobody asked for.
cells.verb: Tending what is growing, by hand, so it holds for whoever comes after

cells.tense: Something you shared with other people ended, and you have not left that place.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Take up the practice you'd most want kept in the world — a line, a page, a meeting — once this week, with no plan past that.
cells.core:
You stepped away from keeping something shared alive. Maybe you moved, maybe the group broke up, maybe the season turned and your hands couldn't hold it. Whatever happened, you've stayed near where it used to grow, and that costs more than it shows.

There's a practice you haven't touched because of what happened around it. Take it up at the smallest size it can be done — one line a week, one page, one hour in a room with whoever comes. You don't need to know whether anyone joins. You need the small act, done regularly. Starting is the whole move. The way back into a shared thing is to keep making your part of it, even before anyone sees.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped making your part, but you haven't moved on.

cells.tense: You are already keeping something alive for others while calling it nobody's job.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Next time you do the quiet thing that keeps a shared practice running, do that one piece where someone nearby can see you.
cells.core:
Someone keeps a shared thing going — the old text gets read, the group stays in touch, the room is set up before anyone walks in — and you'd tell it as something that just happens. It's being done by a person. That person's hands are yours.

Done unseen is how it becomes something no one is doing. This time, do one piece of it where you can be seen. Not a speech, not a claim on it — just where the work happens, in view of someone nearby. You're not after a thank you. You're giving the work a face that has a name on it. That's enough for the thing to be known as tended.
cells.sheetLine: The work is being done. The hand is your hand.
cells.verb: Tending what is growing, by hand, so it holds for whoever comes after
cells.place: Where meaning is passed between people and kept alive by use

attempts.check: The four cores lean on one claim the record does not support: that this person has actually been doing the tending, or failing to, in something shared with others. The record gives the signature and the seat, not the life. A reader could fairly say the tending is somebody else's, or that the thing being stewarded is money, land, or a practice kept privately, not a group's meaning. The asks survive that: each one is a small act the person can do in whatever shared thing they actually hold. The sentence serving me worst is the Unacknowledged core's line about the others knowing who really keeps it — it flatters the reading and tells the person what other people think; it is gone.
